# @zakkster/lite-layout-profiler

Dev-mode forced-reflow detector and budget gate for DOM-binding code.
Version 1.7.0. Zero dependencies. MIT (c) Zahary Shinikchiev.

## What it does

Patches layout-triggering reads (offsetWidth, getBoundingClientRect,
getComputedStyle, SVGGraphicsElement.getBBox / getCTM / getScreenCTM,
scrollIntoView / scrollTo / scrollBy on Element and window, window
innerWidth / innerHeight / scrollX / scrollY / pageXOffset / pageYOffset)
and DOM write methods (style.setProperty, every per-property style
setter on CSSStyleDeclaration.prototype, className, appendChild,
innerHTML, etc.). Flags read-after-write within the same synchronous
task as a forced reflow, times the stall it caused, and can fail a
build over the result.

Per-property style setters (`style.width = 'X'` etc.) are patched
separately from `setProperty()` because in real browsers the WebIDL
per-property setters call C++ internals directly, bypassing the JS
`setProperty` method.

Stack attribution requires unminified code or sourcemaps for readable
readSite / writeSite. Set captureStacks: false to skip stack capture
in busy environments.

## Three lanes

detect (1.0) -- record forced reflows with call-site attribution.
gate   (1.1) -- checkNoReflow / assertNoReflow turn a run into pass/fail.
cost   (1.2) -- time each stall; null when below the clock's granularity.
phase  (1.3) -- classify each reflow by scheduler (raf/timer/microtask/
               ro-callback); gate frame-killers via maxInRaf. Opt-in via
               { phases: true }. Thrash collapsing folds a repeated
               read-after-write tuple into one counted group (maxThrash).

## API

createLayoutProfiler(options?) -- start detecting.
  options: maxStored (integer 1..1000000, default 200; maxViolations is
  the deprecated pre-1.1 name for it), onViolation, captureStacks,
  warnToConsole, ignorePatterns, measureCost (default true), clock.
  Invalid maxStored throws TypeError rather than being coerced.
  clock is only adopted when measureCost is on.

profiler.violations -- chronological snapshot of retained records, with stacks.
profiler.violationCount -- exact total, even if the store was capped.
profiler.summary() -- serialisable snapshot; the gate's input.
profiler.destroy() -- unpatch all prototypes (every realm, main last).
profiler.reset() -- clear records, keep active.
profiler.addRealm(source) -- (v1.7) instrument an additional realm: an iframe's
  contentWindow (same-origin) or a realm-descriptor object { Element, HTMLElement,
  Node, CSSStyleDeclaration, DOMTokenList, SVGGraphicsElement, window } (all
  optional). Returns { available, reason?, realmIndex, remove() }. remove()
  restores JUST that realm (LIFO, idempotent, throw-safe). A cross-origin or
  unusable source degrades to { available:false, reason:'unusable_realm' }, never
  throws, and is not counted toward coverage. summary().patched.realms reports the
  instrumented count (1 = main only). Coverage AND-s across realms; a hole is
  namespaced (realm:1.read:offsetWidth). No auto-follow of navigation, no frame
  discovery, cross-origin unreachable -- documented blind spots, caller names each
  realm.

checkNoReflow(summary, rules?) -- returns a GateReport, never throws on breach.
assertNoReflow(summary, rules?) -- throws ReflowBudgetError on breach.
ReflowBudgetError -- carries .report and .violations.
READ_NAMES -- closed vocabulary of read names this build can emit.
_verdictOf(report) -- derive 'pass'|'fail'|'inconclusive' from a report's
  ok/verified booleans. verified must be exactly true for a definitive verdict;
  anything else is inconclusive (fail-closed).
formatConsole(report) -- human output, ASCII PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE tags.
formatJson(report) -- the lite-layout-report/1 envelope: { schema, version,
  generatedAt, verdict, report }. This is the layout.json the CLI reads.
formatMarkdown(report) -- PR-comment table.
formatGithubAnnotations(report) -- ::error per violation on fail, ::warning on
  inconclusive, empty on pass.
VERSION -- '1.7.0'.

## CLI (v1.6): lite-layout-gate

Layout cannot be forced headless in Node, so the CLI does NOT run the profiler.
The browser runs it, calls checkNoReflow, serialises with formatJson to a
layout.json; the CLI gates that file:

  lite-layout-gate <layout.json> [--format console|json|markdown|github]
                                 [--out path] [--allow-inconclusive]

Exit codes: 0 pass, 1 fail, 2 inconclusive, 3 infrastructure error (missing
file, bad JSON, or a summary rather than a report). No `run` subcommand. Ships
in files[] as bin/LiteLayoutGate.mjs. prepublishOnly gates two checked-in
fixtures produced by the real profiler.

## Violation shape

{ id, taskId, read, write, readSite, writeSite, readStack, writeStack,
  costMs, belowGranularity, phase, roFeedback, timestamp }

phase is the scheduler the reflow fired under (v1.3): raf | timer |
microtask | ro-callback | unknown | unobserved. 'unobserved' means phases
were off; 'unknown' means phases were on but no wrapped scheduler was
active -- never guessed into raf. roFeedback is true inside a
ResizeObserver callback that had already written layout.

taskId is the epoch of the synchronous block, advanced by the microtask
checkpoint that clears the dirty flag. Reflows sharing a taskId happened
in one uninterrupted block.

costMs is milliseconds spent inside the original getter, or null when
unmeasurable. belowGranularity distinguishes "too fast to time" from
"timing was off".

## Summary shape

{ total, stored, truncated, stacks, byRead, byWrite, byTask, taskCount,
  patched: { applied, failed, skipped, foreign, complete, provenance, failures },
  phases: { raf, timer, microtask, roCallback, unknown, unobserved },
  phasesObserved,        -- was requestAnimationFrame actually wrapped
  expected,              -- recorded reflows inside a profiler.expected() scope (v1.5)
  thrash: [ { read, write, taskId, phase, count, costMs } ... ],  -- count>1
  maxThrashCount,        -- worst collapsed count, what maxThrash gates
  cost: { resolutionMs, measured, unmeasured, totalMs, maxMs, avgMs, p99Ms },
  records: [ lean records without stacks ] }

summary.records stays the RAW one-per-reflow view so the gate's counting
is unchanged; thrash is a separate, additive collapsed view.

Coverage (v1.4): patched.foreign counts targets already wrapped by ANOTHER
lite-layout-profiler instance when we instrumented (detected via a wrapper
brand -- a certain signal for another instance). patched.provenance maps
each non-clean target to 'foreign' or 'unknown'. patched.complete is true
only when failed === 0 AND foreign === 0. Honest limit: an UNBRANDED
pre-existing wrapper cannot be told from a pristine host impl by inspection
(happy-dom/jsdom impls have no [native code] marker), so it is NEVER
falsely called foreign. Destroy stacked instances in reverse creation order
(LIFO) or an inner instance's restore is a no-op and leaves an orphan.

Serialisable. Ship it out of the browser as JSON and gate it in a process
that never saw the profiler.

## Gate rules

maxReflows      -- total counted reflows. Default 0.
maxPerTask      -- worst single synchronous block.
maxCostMs       -- worst single measured stall, ms.
maxTotalCostMs  -- sum of measured stalls, ms.
maxInRaf        -- forced reflows inside rAF callbacks (frame-killers).
                   Needs { phases: true } + rAF present, else unverifiable.
maxThrash       -- worst collapsed read-after-write count in any one task.
allowReads      -- exact read names to exclude, validated against READ_NAMES.
allowWrites     -- write-source prefixes to exclude.
ignoreSites     -- call-site substrings to exclude, matches readSite or writeSite.
allowExpected   -- boolean (v1.5). Exclude reflows stamped by profiler.expected(fn),
                   by DYNAMIC SCOPE not read name. Unverifiable on a pre-1.5 summary.

Report: { ok, verified, total, counted, excluded, excludedBy,
          cost: { measured, unmeasured, totalMs, maxMs } | null,
          violations: [{ metric, limit, actual, reason }] }

The violation entry shape is shared with lite-gc-profiler's checkNoGc, so
both profilers report to CI tooling in one vocabulary.

## Fail-closed

Every rule declares the evidence it needs. If the summary cannot supply
it, the rule fails as unverifiable rather than passing, and verified
goes false.

  (every rule)                needs a complete net      fails if patched.complete === false
  maxReflows                  needs summary.total       never unverifiable
  maxPerTask                  needs complete records    fails if truncated
  allowReads / allowWrites    needs complete records    fails if truncated
  ignoreSites                 needs records + sites     also fails if captureStacks: false
  allowExpected               needs record.expected     fails if summary is pre-1.5
  maxCostMs / maxTotalCostMs  needs measured costs      fails if any counted reflow is unmeasured
  maxInRaf                    needs phasesObserved      fails if phases were off or rAF absent
  maxThrash                   needs complete records    fails if truncated

Zero counted reflows through a torn record set is not a clean run.
maxReflows alone survives truncation, because total is kept independently
of the storage ring: a capped run is gateable on volume, not on shape.

Unknown rule keys throw TypeError with a did-you-mean hint rather than
being ignored. Rules from unshipped lanes (maxInTimer, maxInMicrotask) name their lane
and status instead of guessing a spelling. allowReads entries are validated against READ_NAMES.

## Null is not zero

Browsers coarsen performance.now(): non-isolated Chrome clamps to 100us,
Firefox to 1ms. A reflow shorter than that reads back as exactly 0, which
is indistinguishable from free.

The profiler probes the clock floor once at init (cost.resolutionMs). A
stall must exceed MORE THAN ONE TICK to be recorded: a delta of exactly
one tick means the true duration lies in (0, 2 x tick), an interval that
contains zero, so it is not a lower bound at all. Anything at or below one
tick is costMs: null with belowGranularity: true.

Aggregates follow: with measured === 0, totalMs / maxMs / avgMs / p99Ms
are all null, never 0. resolutionMs null means the floor could not be
determined at all.

Consequence: on a coarse-clocked browser, cost budgets do not apply and
you gate on counts instead. You cannot pass a budget you could not measure.

## ignorePatterns vs ignoreSites

ignorePatterns (profiler option) drops a reflow at capture time -- never
recorded, never in total.
ignoreSites (gate rule) excludes an already-recorded reflow at gate time
-- still in total, subtraction visible in excluded / excludedBy.

Expected-scope lane (v1.5): profiler.expected(fn) marks a SYNCHRONOUS
region as a deliberate-measurement zone (FLIP reads, virtualised-list
sizing). Reflows inside it are stamped record.expected=true; allowExpected
excuses them by DYNAMIC SCOPE, so the SAME read is allowed where you meant
it and still fails elsewhere -- strictly finer than allowReads, which
silences a read everywhere. Synchronous only: an await inside the callback
escapes the scope (a reflow after await is a new task). The label is inert
until a gate opts in; the scope labels records, never suppresses them, so
summary().records keeps every expected reflow for audit. excludedBy.expected
counts them; overlap with an identity rule is excluded once.

Prefer ignoreSites so the number stays honest.

WARNING: ignorePatterns is a raw substring match against the captured
stack. In a browser every frame is a file URL, so a pattern like
'index.html' or 'app' matches your own code's frames and silently drops
every reflow -- counter stuck at 0. Target a dependency path
('node_modules/gsap'), never a generic word or your own file path. Node
stacks often lack URLs, so this hides in tests and only bites in Chrome.

## Detection mechanism

Write sets a dirty flag with queueMicrotask auto-clear; the same
checkpoint advances taskEpoch.
Read while dirty = forced reflow. The read is timed across the original
getter. Flag clears after the first flagged read (layout was
recalculated). Next write re-dirties.

Records live in a fixed-size ring, so overflow never moves an element.
The newest maxStored records are retained.

## CI-counting configuration

createLayoutProfiler({ captureStacks: false, measureCost: false })
-- no stack allocation, no timing. Cost rules become unverifiable;
maxReflows and maxPerTask keep working.

## Dev-mode only

Patches prototypes. Allocates per violation (record object, and
Error.stack when captureStacks is on). NOT zero-GC. Ship behind a
__DEV__ flag or strip in production.

## Patch coverage

This library modifies its host, so it can be refused. A frozen prototype
or a non-configurable descriptor means a read goes uninstrumented, and a
detector with holes reports zero for the same reason a working one does.

summary().patched = { applied, failed, skipped, complete, failures }

  applied  instrumented
  skipped  absent from this host -- not a hole, nothing flows through a
           path the host does not have
  failed   present and refused -- a real hole
  complete failed === 0

complete: false makes every gate rule unverifiable at once.

Teardown is identity-checked: a restore only fires if the current value
is still the wrapper this profiler installed, so destroy() never deletes
a foreign instrumenter that patched on top.

## Reentrancy

onViolation fires synchronously inside the offending task. The dirty flag
is cleared BEFORE the callback runs, so a callback that reads layout does
not trigger itself, and a callback that throws does not strand the flag.
Treat the callback like an interrupt handler: record, do not render.

## Testing

npm test -- runs test/*.test.mjs and test/torture/*.test.mjs
415 tests (223 main + 192 torture). Main: 01-detect, 02-gate,
03-gate-live, 04-cost, 05-cost-live, 06-phase, 07-provenance,
08-expected, 09-report, 10-cli, 11-realm, 12-viewer, 13-coverage-holes,
14-mocks.
Torture: l1-5-patching, l2-5-gate-adversarial, l3-5-cost-clock,
l4-5-phase, l4-6-provenance, l5-5-expected, l6-5-report-cli, l7-5-realm,
l99-9-extreme -- adversarial scenarios across nine axes, see TORTURE.md.
The live suites drive the real patcher against a stub DOM with an
injected clock, so timer-resolution behaviour is deterministic.
